hints: Use Newton's second law in the direction of motion: $F_D - R = ma$ to find the driving force $F_D$.
Substitute $m = 1800\text{ kg}$, $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $R = 650\text{ N}$.
Calculate power using $P = F_D v$ with $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
State Newton's second law in the forward horizontal direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$

Substitute the given mass $m = 1800\text{ kg}$, acceleration $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and resistance $R = 650\text{ N}$:
$$F_D - 650 = 1800 \times 0.5$$
$$F_D - 650 = 900$$
Add $650$ to both sides to find the driving force:
$$F_D = 900 + 650 = 1550\text{ N}$$

State the relationship between power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 1550\text{ N}$ and speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 1550 \times 20 = 31000\text{ W} = 31\text{ kW}$$

hints: Steady speed implies zero acceleration, so driving force equals resistance: $F_D = 650\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F_D v$ with constant power $P = 31000\text{ W}$ and solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
At steady (constant) speed on a horizontal road, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), which means the net horizontal force must be zero:
$$F_D = R = 650\text{ N}$$

State the power equation in terms of driving force and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies v = \frac{P}{F_D}$$

Substitute power $P = 31000\text{ W}$ and driving force $F_D = 650\text{ N}$:
$$v = \frac{31000}{650}$$

Simplify the fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by $50$:
$$v = \frac{620}{13} \approx 47.7\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
